Shock_Description: No shock. Portfolio assumptions as configured, correlation as configured. The comparator every other scenario is read against.
Rationale: Not a forecast. A reference point - the scenario in which nothing in particular happens, which is itself unlikely.

Shock_Description: Policy and long rates rise 300bp. Senior coupon reprices; the concessional layer has to work harder for the same mobilisation.
Rationale: LIT-012 and LIT-013: the junior tranche is the mobilisation lever, and its required size moves with the return private capital demands. The modest default multiplier reflects second-order pressure on borrowers via local lending rates rather than a direct channel - most PL-1 loans are fixed-charge and short, so a rate move does not hit the existing book directly.

Shock_Description: Staple food prices rise sharply, on the scale of the 2007-08 and 2010-11 episodes visible in the MAC-06 history.
Rationale: The most direct macro-to-repayment channel for PL-1 (Memo 1). Critically this is a CORRELATED shock - it hits a whole region at once - so correlation is overridden upward rather than left at the base. Recovery falls because distressed borrowers in a distressed region have less to recover from.

Shock_Description: Sustained oil price spike. Feeds the PL-2 tariff and procurement environment, and pushes fuel and fertiliser costs into food prices.
Rationale: One of the few drivers that moves both product lines at once (PL-2 doc, OQ-8). Worth modelling precisely because the diversification case for running both lines assumes shared drivers are rare.

Shock_Description: Local currency depreciates 25% against the hard currency the notes are denominated in.
Rationale: Named as a live risk in the business plan. Local-currency receivables against a hard-currency tranche is an unhedged mismatch; the default multiplier captures import-price pass-through to borrowers, not the translation loss itself - that is applied at the tranche level, not the loan level.

Shock_Description: Rates up, food prices up and currency down together. Not a forecast - a coherence test.
Rationale: These drivers are not independent in the real world: a rate-hiking cycle, a commodity spike and EM currency pressure have historically arrived together. A structure that only survives them one at a time has not been stress tested.
